meta.home.description: md2pdf — free, no-login tool to convert a GitHub README or Markdown into a polished PDF. Paste a repo URL, preview, print to PDF.

home.tagline: by LadeStack · free · no login · client-side
home.hero.lead: Paste a repository URL and md2pdf fetches the README, resolves its images and badges, and lays the whole thing out for paper — all inside your browser.
home.converter.title: Converter
home.converter.lead: Three ways in — a repository URL, a Markdown file, or the keyboard. The preview is the document.
home.converter.hint: Pulls the README (tries main/master plus case variants), resolves relative images and badges, and renders below. Private repos aren't supported.
home.converter.placeholder: # Paste Markdown here, or fetch a repo above…
home.converter.darkWarn: Dark reads well on screen but prints poorly — we auto-lighten it for print and PDF.
home.converter.toc: Auto table of contents (docs with 3+ headings)
home.converter.printHint: Export uses your browser's print-to-PDF (100% client-side). Choose “Save as PDF” in the print dialog.
home.book.title: Documentation book
home.book.lead: Point at a repository, choose the Markdown files that belong together, and print one paginated book — cover, master contents, and every chapter in the order you set.
home.book.hint: Finds README, {code:.md}, {code:.markdown}, and {code:.mdown} files, including folders. A book holds at most 30 files; public repositories only.
home.book.subtitlePlaceholder: A short description for the cover
home.book.chaptersHint: Print order follows this list. Use the arrow buttons to move a chapter, or × to remove it.
home.book.chaptersEmpty: Chapters appear here after a scan.
home.book.failuresTitle: Some files could not be loaded
home.book.printHint: A book prints only when every selected chapter has loaded. Export uses your browser's print-to-PDF — choose “Save as PDF” in the dialog.
home.book.exportLead: Create one PDF for every built chapter and pack them into a ZIP archive. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
home.book.exportLimit: Up to 30 PDFs and 128 MB per ZIP.
home.book.exportPartial: Export finished; {files} could not be rendered.
home.book.exportFailed: The export failed. Nothing was downloaded.
home.book.exportReadyHint: Keep this tab open until the download begins.
home.book.exportSingle: Each chapter becomes its own PDF inside the ZIP, with its folder path preserved.
home.book.exportWarning: Some content was simplified: unsupported characters are shown as ? and inaccessible images are skipped.
home.book.exportStale: The book changed. Build it again before exporting.
home.book.exportBuildFirst: Build the book before exporting PDFs.
home.book.exportFontsFailed: The PDF fonts could not be downloaded. Check your connection and try again.
home.book.exportTooLarge: The ZIP would exceed the 128 MB limit. Select fewer or smaller files.
home.statement.body: The only network call the tool makes is an anonymous read of the public README you asked for. Everything else — rendering, sanitising, printing — happens on your machine.
home.how.title: How it works
home.how.lead: Three steps, no account, no server-side renderer.
home.how.step1.title: Give it a repository
home.how.step1.body: A full URL, a bare {code:owner/repo}, or a link with extra path segments — all three resolve to the same repo.
home.how.step2.title: Watch it render
home.how.step2.body: Markdown becomes HTML in the browser, sanitised by DOMPurify, with a table of contents when the document warrants one.
home.how.step3.title: Print to PDF
home.how.step3.body: Hit export, choose “Save as PDF”, and you have a clean, paginated document — no watermark, no upload.
home.themes.title: Four print themes
home.themes.lead: Each theme is a print stylesheet, not a colour swap — pick the register your document wants.
home.themes.clean: Neutral sans, the default for specs and READMEs.
home.themes.business: Serif headings and a dark code block for reports.
home.themes.academic: Justified serif pages for long-form prose.
home.themes.dark: Screen-first; auto-lightens for print so nothing is lost.
home.features.title: What it handles
home.features.lead: The unglamorous details that make a README printable.
home.features.fetch1.title: Ten filename candidates.
home.features.fetch1.body: README.md, readme.md, README.MD and the rest, including {code:.github/}.
home.features.fetch2.title: Branch discovery.
home.features.fetch2.body: The default branch is read from the API, with {code:main} and {code:master} as fallbacks.
home.features.fetch3.title: Graceful degradation.
home.features.fetch3.body: A rate-limited API still lets the raw fetch continue.
home.features.fetch4.title: Every URL form.
home.features.fetch4.body: {code:owner/repo}, {code:.git} suffixes, and links that point at a file or folder.
home.features.render1.title: Relative paths.
home.features.render1.body: Images point at raw content, document links point at the blob view, and traversal is clamped at the repo root.
home.features.render2.title: Code stays intact.
home.features.render2.body: Fenced blocks and inline spans are never rewritten.
home.features.render3.title: GitHub-flavoured Markdown.
home.features.render3.body: Tables, task lists, strikethrough and fenced code all render.
home.features.render4.title: Sanitised output.
home.features.render4.body: Scripts, styles, frames and forms are stripped before anything reaches the page.
home.privacy.title: Private by construction
home.privacy.lead: There is no backend to upload to. Your Markdown is read, rendered and printed on your own device — the only bytes that leave are the public README files you asked for.

# md2pdf — Sample README

Paste a GitHub repo URL above, drop a `README.md`, or just type Markdown here.

## Features

- [x] GitHub URL fetch with image/badge path resolution
- [x] Live GFM preview (tables, task lists, code)
- [ ] Your next great README section

## Table demo

| Option | What it does |
| ------ | ------------ |
| Clean  | Neutral default |
| Dark   | Screen-friendly (auto-lightens for print) |

## Code demo

```js
const msg = "hello readme";
console.log(msg);
```

## Links & images

A relative image like `docs/logo.png` resolves against the fetched repo.
An absolute badge like ![build](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-brightgreen) is left untouched.
